conviction_note: Nothing company-level and unpriced turned up. Peers that reported after MAN's 16 July guide (Randstad 22 Jul, Adecco 6 Aug) said momentum carried into early Q3. French temp work in August is flat (-0.3% y/y), which sits inside MAN's 'flat to slight growth' France guide. US series disagree (BLS temp help down, Bullhorn hours up 7-11%) on a segment that is 15% of revenue. Euro translation runs slightly ahead of the guide-date rate. Short interest is about 9.5% of shares out with 5.4 days to cover, after an -11.6% 20-day pullback. The sum is a small +0.6. Scaled, p_up 54 times abs 9.25 (option-implied, with the name's fat 32/19/15-point tails and a new Q4 guide) gives +0.74. The two measurements agree in sign and size, because both rest on proxies that mostly land inside what the company already guided.
bar: Q3 adjusted EPS: company guide $0.96-1.06, midpoint $1.01 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000871763/000119312526305399/man-ex99_1.htm). Consensus $1.01 on revenue $4.85bn (Benzinga, https://www.benzinga.com/node/62129617) and $1.01 (Earnings Whispers, https://beta.earningswhispers.com/go/w/MAN): two estimate sources agree, plus the guide. Q3 revenue guide is +3% to +7% cc, about 6% organic days-adjusted at midpoint (Q2 call transcript, https://www.mitrade.com/insights/news/live-news/article-8-1929502-20260723). print_vs_bar_pct is measured on revenue against $4.85bn.
positioning_check: Short interest 4,426,985 shares at the 2026-09-30 FINRA settlement, 5.38 days to cover, down from a 6,748,967 peak on 2026-06-30. That is about 9.5% of 46.51m shares outstanding (Equibles, https://equibles.com/stocks/man/short-interest, read 2026-10-14). The July print squeezed +32% off a 6.3-6.7m share short base. Skew: skew_25d_vol_points is null in the baseline, so the market makes no directional statement. Put/call OI is 0.98 and the event-implied move is 9.25%. Moderately crowded, not extreme. It shrinks any negative and supports a small upside asymmetry.

findings.finding: Both large European peers reported after MAN's 16 July guide and said growth momentum carried into Q3. Randstad (22 Jul 2026) said 'growth momentum continued into early Q3 2026, with most markets in growth and activity improving'. Adecco (6 Aug 2026) printed +5.6% organic and flagged continued volume momentum into early August. Both support MAN's ~6% organic midpoint.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: MAN's revenue and guide surprise moves have been large. 2026-07-16: +32.37% on a beat plus an above-consensus guide. 2025-04-17: -19.07%. 2025-10-16: -6.52% (baseline history). A confirmation of an in-line guide has historically produced small moves (2026-04-16 +0.88%, 2025-01-30 +0.55%).
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced. Both statements are 10-12 weeks old, and MAN rallied to near a $63 52-week high after them. If the stock were still pricing a slowdown it would not have doubled off its low (+98.97% from the 52w low per baseline). It only supports the midpoint, inside the guide, so its value is a small tilt against a miss.
findings.independence: Adecco Q2 2026 results, 2026-08-06 (https://www.adeccogroup.com/en/our-group/media/press-releases/q2-2026-results): a different company, different document, same direction. Both are peer read-throughs, not MAN numbers.

findings.finding: French temp employment, MAN's largest country at ~24% of Q2 revenue, was down 0.3% y/y in August 2026 at 623,070 FTE (Prism'emploi, published 2026-10-08). That is in line with MAN France's 0.0% cc in Q2 and with the 'flat to slight growth' Q3 France guide, if anything at its low edge.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: France has been flat to slightly negative for MAN through 2025-26 without itself driving the reaction. The large moves have come from group guidance and margins (baseline history).
findings.why_not_priced: Released a week ago and lands inside the company's own France guide. A market pricing a French miss would show a sharp France-specific derating; the -11.6% 20-day fall has no stated French cause. Sized near zero because it confirms the guide.
findings.independence: Insee Q2 2026 temp employment -1.7% y/y (https://www.insee.fr/fr/statistiques/fichier/version-html/9039152/IR214-Emploi-2T-2026.pdf), while MAN France ran 0.0% cc in Q2. So MAN has been tracking above the national series, which argues against reading the August print as a MAN miss. Proxy only.

findings.finding: The US temp series disagree over Q3, on a segment that is ~15% of revenue and that MAN guided to grow at about Q2's ~6%. BLS temp help fell 10,900 in September, and July was revised to -10,000 (SIA summary of the 2026-10-02 BLS release). The SIA/Bullhorn hours indicator showed US staffing hours +7% to +11% y/y through September, industrial +12% to +17%. Netted toward the broader BLS series, the result is near zero.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The US segment was cited as a contributor to the July beat (+32.37%), alongside the group guide. No record of a US-only surprise moving the stock on its own.
findings.why_not_priced: The BLS print is twelve days old and sits inside the stock's -11.6% 20-day fall, so it is plausibly already in the price. The Bullhorn indicator is behind a paywall and little quoted, but it is the narrower series. Net of the rest of the company (85% non-US), either reading moves group revenue by well under 1%.
findings.independence: SIA/Bullhorn Staffing Indicator, weeks to 2026-09-26 (https://www.staffingindustry.com/news/global-daily-news/staffing-hours-reach-new-year-to-date-high-in-week-of-sept-26-sia-bullhorn-staffing-indicator) points the opposite way. The two were merged into one finding because they describe the same line.

findings.finding: EUR/USD averaged about 1.151 over Q3 2026 (Jul 1.1425, Aug 1.1592, Sep 1.1511) against about 1.144 on the 16 July guide date. Translation therefore ran slightly better than the rate implied when MAN set its '2c unfavourable FX' assumption, worth a fraction of a cent of EPS.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: FX has never been the cause of a MAN reaction in the baseline history.
findings.why_not_priced: Every model can compute this, and it is too small to show in the price. Filed for completeness as a macro-to-company transmission. The exact FX assumption on the guidance slide was not retrieved.

findings.finding: Into the print, short interest is 4.43m shares, about 9.5% of shares outstanding, with 5.38 days to cover (FINRA 2026-09-30 via Equibles). The stock is -11.6% over 20 days and 18.6% below its 52-week high. The last print squeezed +32% off a similar short base, so the reaction is skewed toward upside on anything in line.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: 2026-07-16: +32.37% with ~6.3m shares short (2026-07-15 settlement) after a long drawdown. 2026-01-29: +14.95%. Five of seven prints in the baseline were up.
findings.why_not_priced: Short interest has been falling (6.75m to 4.43m), so part of the squeeze fuel is gone. The option market shows no skew statement (null), and put/call OI is 0.98. If the market priced squeeze risk fully, calls would trade rich to puts, and nothing in the baseline shows that.

baseline_tension: The baseline carries no skew. The -11.6% run-up into the print and a ~9.5% short base leave room for a squeeze, and the small positive lean agrees with that positioning rather than cutting against it. Nothing found is company-level, so p_up stays near 50.
lessons_applied: Rules 1 and 6 (inside the guide): the peer-momentum finding confirms MAN's guided ~6% midpoint, so +0.5 became +0.3.
Rule 6 (inside the guide): French August temp work lands inside the 'flat to slight growth' France guide, so -0.2 became -0.1.

Rule 5 (narrow proxy loses to broad series): the US finding was netted toward the broader BLS temp-help series rather than the narrower Bullhorn hours indicator, so +0.2 became -0.1. Rule 9 kept it small, since the US is ~15% of revenue.
Rule 8 (understatement): abs_move_pct raised from 9.0 to the full 9.25 event-implied move, given the 32/19/15-point tails in the name's own history.
Rule 7 (positioning): short interest was checked before any negative and is recorded. The +0.4 positioning finding was left standing.
p_up moved from 55 to 54, because the remaining lean rests on proxies and positioning inside the guide. print_vs_bar moved from +0.5 to +0.3.
